newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish clerics told to preach against soil erosion.
newsitem.headline: Turkish clerics told to preach against soil erosion.

text.p: Turkish Moslem clerics are to encourage their congregations to plant trees to fight soil erosion, Islamic officials said on Thursday.
The department of religious affairs said in a statement it had sent a circular to "imams", or clerics, urging them to build sermons around the dangers of erosion.
"Among the chief rules of our great religion is the protection of green places, the planting of trees, the virtue of growing fruit and not polluting water," the circular said.
The department said erosion was the greatest threat facing Turkey, with levels 17 times greater than in Europe. It said the equivalent of 150,000 lorry loads of earth were lost in Turkey every day.

"The muftu (provincial Moslem leaders) and the imams (local clerics) should give the congregation in their sermons, enlightening information on the importance of planting trees, the value of woodlands and protecting our national heritage," the statement said.

Moslem clerics should should set an example by planting trees and publicising their efforts on radio and television, the message said. The department said it awaited a report detailing their activities by the end of July.
